# kodawari

> kodawari turns a written spec into finished, tested code — autonomously, and it
> proves every step instead of just claiming it. You give it a markdown file
> describing a feature; it plans, writes the code, runs your tests, has a second
> AI model review the result, fixes what review flags, and stops at a ship/no-ship
> decision. A pipeline, not a chat.

What makes it different: three separate LLM roles (planner, reviewer, executor)
so no model grades its own work; a strict no-fake-run guarantee (under
`KODAWARI_REVIEW_ENABLED=1`, "tests passed" means pytest really ran and a second
model really approved — unverifiable steps fail closed); a contract-first audit
trail where every step is a JSON-schema-validated artifact; and cross-run memory
that learns recurring failure patterns and shares portable lessons across
projects via `~/.kodawari/instincts.json`. Greenfield is first-class (empty dir +
spec → scaffolded, tested feature); large specs split into resumable slices. It's
a headless, CI-friendly alternative to interactive AI pair-programmers like Claude
Code, Cursor, Aider, and OpenHands. Python 3.11+, MIT licensed, public beta
(v0.1.2).
